screens.prompt: In B7, count how many of the five steps have a date in B2:B6.

hints.syntax: Start with = and close the bracket: =COUNTA(B2:B6).
hints.func-counta: The dates sit in a text column, so COUNT finds no numbers at all. COUNTA counts anything that is not blank.
hints.require-ref: Point COUNTA at B2:B6. Pasting the three dates in would freeze the count at the progress of the day you wrote it.
hints.value: Two of the five cells are empty, so the answer is the other three.
hints.error: One of these cells may hold a space rather than a date, which COUNTA counts as done.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
COUNT looks for numbers and the dates are text, so it answers zero
there is nothing to add up, and adding is not counting
a count divided by zero returns #DIV/0!
the dates typed into the formula, so the count stops following the sheet
the range stops before Publish and Archive, so two dated steps are left out
the count is three; adding one to it reports four

docs.explain:
COUNTA counts the cells in a range that hold something, whatever it is: a date, a word, a space. Only empty cells are left out. Three of the five cells in B2:B6 hold a date, so the answer is 3.

COUNT asks the narrower question and returns 0 on this column, because the dates sit in it as text rather than as date values. On a checklist the empty cells carry the meaning: each one is a step nobody has started, and the filled ones are the progress report.

A cell holding a single space counts as filled. Clean the stray spaces out of a checklist and the total drops to the number of steps really finished.

errors.text: A cell with a space typed into it counts as filled, so progress rises without any work being done.
COUNT over B2:B6 answers 0, because it looks for numbers and the dates are text.
COUNTA typed with an extra letter is not a function Excel knows, so the cell shows an error.

docs.atWork: A launch checklist where each empty cell is a step still to do and the dated ones are what the status deck reports.
docs.outcome: Count filled cells rather than numbers, so a checklist reports real progress.

seo.title: COUNTA in Excel: count non-empty cells
seo.description: Three dates and two blanks. COUNTA answers 3 because it counts anything filled, while COUNT answers 0 since these entries arrived as text.
